messages:
Sasha: Hey team — customer opened a ticket saying they saw 500s and high latency but couldn't find any request/trace id to send us. They only saw a vague 'trace token' in the product UI. Can someone confirm exact places customers should look (Console, SDKs, headers) and a minimal repro checklist?
Liam: Short answer: we expect either a request id in response headers (x-redwood-request-id / x-redwood-trace-id), a trace id in the Console logs, or an SDK error object that includes requestId. If none are present, ask for a HAR or a curl or timestamps. :white_check_mark:
Alex: Console -> Logs -> choose time window -> click the request row -> in the right-hand pane copy "trace_id" (top) or "request_id" under headers. For older Console views there's a "Share debug bundle" button in the top-right of the logs panel.
Alex: SDKs: Node/Python/Go/JS SDKs put request ids on errors as `err.requestId` or as `response.headers['x-redwood-request-id']`. Mobile SDKs log `request_id=...` to device logs (Logcat / NSLog). If customer uses our embed SDK, look for `X-Redwood-Request` header in outbound requests (case-insensitive).
Sasha: Can you paste a short curl example we can give customers so they can reproduce and include the header?
Alex: Yep — give them this minimal reproduction (ask them to replace $API_KEY and payload):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Alex: When curl runs with `-v` they should see response headers. Ask them to copy any `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-redwood-trace-id` values. If nothing appears, ask them to add an explicit header to help correlate on our side: `-H "x-client-request-id: <their-id>"` and include that id in the ticket.
Maya: Browser repros — ask for a HAR export from Chrome: DevTools -> Network -> right click -> Save all as HAR. Also include a screenshot of the Network row showing status and any response headers. For single-call JS SDK repros, a tiny snippet that reproduces the call is helpful.
Liam: Mobile repros — for Android get `adb logcat` around the time of the request and search for `request_id` or `redwood`. For iOS look for `NSLog` lines from our SDK. If they used a proxy (Charles/Fiddler), ask for the exported session.
Sasha: Debug bundle flow — Console -> Support -> Create debug bundle -> include: request logs, SDK logs (if attached), config snapshot. That generates a short debug token (dbg_*). Tell customer to paste that token here. We can then attach server-side logs and find the exact request.
Sasha: Also ask for: exact timestamps (UTC), API key prefix (not full key), region, model name, and minimal payload. If billing/auth error, ask for the error body JSON and the response status code.
Alex: Quick correlation tips for us: if they provide a client-generated id (x-client-request-id), we can grep logs directly. If they only provide a timestamp window and workspace/org id, include those too.
Support Bot: Checklist for escalation (paste this to customer):
- Response headers (copy raw headers from curl or browser)
- Any SDK error object JSON (paste)
- HAR (browser) or exported proxy session (Charles/Fiddler)
- Minimal curl snippet used and `-v` output
- Debug bundle token from Console (if possible)
- UTC timestamps +/- 2 minutes of failure and region

Sasha: Thanks — I'll send this checklist to the customer and request a debug bundle + HAR. If they only have a screenshot, ask them to at least copy any header values and the error JSON. :pray:
